I am an old woman of eighty years, and this small piece of land behind my house is where I plant my yam and cocoyam together with some vegetables, as my mother taught me long ago. I have no money to buy the chemical fertilizer from the market — it is too costly for a widow like me — so I use the droppings from my goats and the ash from my cooking fire to feed the soil. My grandchildren help me when they come from school, and sometimes I pay a young man from the village small money to help me make the heaps, because my back cannot do that work anymore.
